en.title: Maximum Primary Capacity With One-to-One Primary/Backup Server Pairing
en.description:
Choose an even number of the n servers: half of them are primaries and half are backups. Each server is used only once, and every primary is paired with a backup whose capacity is at least its own. The contribution is the sum of all primary capacities; find its maximum. You do not have to use all servers.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains memory. 2≤n≤200000, 1≤memory[i]≤10^9. The original constraints mistakenly named the variable size, but their original side note clearly refers to memory; this site uses one name throughout.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 1 and 5 respectively. In the third example, pair 4 with 3 and 2 with 2; the primary capacity is 3+2=5, and 1 is left unused.
hints: Sort capacities in descending order and group adjacent items in pairs, making the smaller one the primary; sum items 2, 4, …, and with an odd count leave the smallest item unused.
